concepts.title: Cubes of Numbers
concepts.definition: A cube is a number multiplied by itself twice more - n cubed equals n times n times n; cubes of even numbers stay even, of odd numbers stay odd, and numbers like 1, 8, 27, 64 that come from natural numbers are perfect cubes.
concepts.key_idea: Triple the self-multiplication: 4 cubed is 64, keeping the parity of its root.
question_patterns: find the cube of 12
is 243 a perfect cube - justify
which of the given numbers are perfect cubes
find the cube of the given rational number
check the parity of the cube of an odd number
express 512 as a cube of a natural number

solution_steps.explain: n times n times n gives the cube.

concepts.title: Adding Consecutive Odd Numbers Gives Cubes
concepts.definition: Cubes hide odd-number patterns: 2 cubed equals 3 plus 5, 3 cubed equals 7 plus 9 plus 11 - each cube is the sum of as many consecutive odd numbers as its root, starting from the right place.
concepts.key_idea: The cube of n is the sum of n consecutive odd numbers - a cube's secret staircase.
question_patterns: express 4 cubed as the sum of consecutive odd numbers
which consecutive odd numbers add to 6 cubed
how many odd numbers make the cube of 5
verify the odd number pattern for 3 cubed
state the pattern connecting cubes and odd numbers
find the sum of the required consecutive odd numbers for the given cube

solution_steps.explain: The cube of n needs exactly n consecutive odd numbers.
Each cube's run of odd numbers starts just past the previous cube's run.
Adding the run reproduces the cube.

concepts.title: Smallest Multiple That Is a Perfect Cube
concepts.definition: Prime factorisation exposes near-cubes: group the prime factors in triples, and any factor left unpaired tells the smallest multiplier - or divisor - that turns the number into a perfect cube, as 81 times 3 becomes 243, the cube of 9.
concepts.key_idea: Triples of prime factors make a cube; the lonely factors name the fix.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh106.txt section 6.2.2 (smallest multiple that is a perfect cube)
question_patterns: find the smallest number by which 81 must be multiplied to get a perfect cube

what cube does the corrected number become

solution_steps.explain: Write the number as a product of prime factors.
Complete triples confirm cube-hood; leftovers do not.
Multiply or divide by the primes that complete or clear the broken triples.

concepts.title: Cube Roots
concepts.definition: The cube root undoes cubing: the cube root of 1331 is 11 because 11 cubed gives 1331; it is found through prime factorisation by taking one factor from every triple, and the method extends to negative numbers and to estimating between known cubes.
concepts.key_idea: One factor from each triple of primes reassembles the root.
concepts.textbook_ref: hemh106.txt section 6.3 (cube roots, prime factorisation method)
question_patterns: find the cube root of 1331 by prime factorisation

solution_steps.explain: Raising to the one-third power undoes the cube.

solution_template.explain: n cubed is n times n times n.
